question: A 71-year-old African American man diagnosed with high blood pressure presents to the outpatient clinic. In the clinic, his blood pressure is 161/88 mm Hg with a pulse of 88/min. He has had similar blood pressure measurements in the past, and you initiate captopril. He presents back shortly after initiation with extremely swollen lips, tongue, and face. After captopril is discontinued, what is the most appropriate step for the management of his high blood pressure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Angioedema due to captopril -> Discontinue captopril -> Consider alternative antihypertensive -> 95% CHAIN: Angioedema due to captopril -> Discontinue captopril -> Initiate an ARB as an alternative -> 90% CHAIN: Angioedema due to captopril -> Discontinue captopril -> Switch to ramipril as an alternative -> 95%
analysis: The patient experienced angioedema, a known side effect of ACE inhibitors like captopril. It is crucial to avoid reinitiating captopril or any other ACE inhibitor due to the high risk of recurrence of angioedema. Instead, an alternative antihypertensive medication should be chosen.
